purpose: The measured readiness of every Super Administrator contract page at UI-08 Increment 1, before any UI-08 source change. Each row records what the canonical authority requires, what the repository actually provides, and the classification that decides the UI-08 action.

classification_legend.B: real capability exists but the route/page is consolidated
classification_legend.D: backend delivery gap closed by an authorized corrective contract over existing substrate
classification_legend.E: legitimately disabled by a closed external gate
classification_legend.F: no backend capability, no canonical permission key and no owning backend phase (superseded by COR-UI08-001 — no page remains in this class)

product_owner_decision.outcome: Option A — authorize the minimum backend enablement for all four former Category F pages.
product_owner_decision.effect: The four pages are reclassified from F to D with COR-UI08-001 as their corrective backend owner. Their original measured gap fields are preserved unchanged below: the gap was real and the Increment 1 stop was correct. Reclassification records an authorized route to delivery, NOT an implementation that already exists.

classification_totals_at_increment_1.note: The measured classification before COR-UI08-001 was recorded. Retained so the original finding is not rewritten.

pages.title: Dashboard
pages.current_browser_proof: none — UI-07 removed the false platform.dashboard placeholder route

pages.title: Subscription Operations
pages.readiness_rationale: D — existing Phase 20B data; corrective platform read projection.
measured_gaps: No platform-scope permission key: the matrix has no platform.subscription.* or platform.invoice.* key. subscription.* and merchant.subscription.* are merchant-scope keys granted to merchant_admin/finance, not super_admin.
No platform-wide API: subscription.show and subscription-invoices.index sit inside the merchant tenant-context group and are scoped to the caller's merchant.
Directive §23.1 forbids mapping this page to a close-enough key such as platform.merchant.view.
pages.measured_gap_resolution: The product owner resolved the permission question directly rather than by agent inference: COR-UI08-001 §7.2 rules that this page IS a platform-wide read-only merchant-governance projection and that platform.merchant.view is therefore its correct primary key, not a close-enough substitute. No platform.subscription.* key is created because the page has no subscription mutation.
pages.ui08_action: Implement under COR-UI08-001 §10 as a read-only projection over existing Phase 20B truth (merchant_subscriptions, scheduled_plan_changes, subscription_invoices, subscription_invoice_items, the existing credit authority, existing escalation/audit events). No new table, no second billing-status state machine, no invoice recomputation, and no mutation endpoint. Every collection paginated, allowlisted sorts, validated and indexed filters, masked. An index is added only after a proven query-plan need.

pages.title: Internal Platform Access
pages.readiness_rationale: D — existing identity/MFA/session/permission substrate; corrective platform access lifecycle contract.
measured_gaps: No permission key for platform-user administration exists among the 167 keys.

No API: routes/api.php registers no platform user invite/suspend/reactivate/deactivate/session-revoke endpoint. The identity routes under /auth are ownership-scoped to the caller and deliberately add no cross-user administration (routes/api.php:150-154).

pages.ui08_action: Implement under COR-UI08-001 §11. This is the only one of the four that adds permission keys — exactly two, both platform-scope, super_admin default, MFA required, manage requiring fresh step-up. Reuses users, Magic Link authentication, MFA enrolment, R6 session families and the existing permission override model; adds only the missing lifecycle substrate (platform_access_memberships, platform_access_invitations, platform_access_permission_overrides) where no canonical equivalent safely carries it. Launch role model is super_admin only. Server-enforced self-protection: no self-escalation, no merchant role or membership assignment, no lockout of the final active Super Administrator.
pages.implementation_status_at_authorization: planned — transitions to implemented only after its real API, permission mapping, route, component, tests and browser proof exist

pages.title: Feature Flags
pages.readiness_rationale: D — approved product capability; corrective platform rollout-governance contract.
measured_gaps: No permission key for feature-flag administration exists among the 167 keys.
No API, no table, no service. `Servana Software Development Plan.md` contains no feature-flag capability at all; only `Servana Project Scope.md` line 245 asserts it.

The navigation contract already carries a per-entry `feature_flag` field and navigationFilter.ts already hides an entry naming an absent flag, so the consuming mechanism exists — the administration surface and its source of truth do not.
pages.measured_gap_resolution: The Plan/Scope difference was the product owner's to resolve and they resolved it in favour of the Scope: the capability is approved and is delivered as a specialized platform-settings governance surface under the existing platform.settings.view/update keys. No feature-flag permission key is created.
pages.ui08_action: Implement under COR-UI08-001 §12. A feature flag is an ADDITIONAL RESTRICTIVE rollout control, never an authorization mechanism. Catalogue is a code-reviewed allowlist (config/platform-feature-flags.php); the API never creates arbitrary keys and rejects unknown ones. Adds platform_feature_flags, platform_feature_flag_targets, platform_feature_flag_change_requests and append-only platform_feature_flag_history. Production-sensitive changes require maker/checker with requester != approver, impact statement, rollback plan, reason, MFA and fresh step-up. Server-side evaluation fails closed: allowlist -> environment -> external gate -> flag state -> effective dates -> target -> rollout, with authorization, entitlement and billing state enforced separately. If the repository holds no approved production flag definitions, the catalogue is truthfully empty and the page shows a real empty state — no fake flags are seeded.
pages.implementation_status_at_authorization: planned — transitions to implemented only after its real API, permission mapping, route, component, tests and browser proof exist
pages.blocked_by_at_increment_1: no permission key, no table, no API, and no Development Plan capability
pages.entry_condition_at_increment_1: the product owner resolves the Plan/Scope difference and authorizes a feature-flag backend phase, including its permission keys and schema
